metadata.scenario_context: Bella, Anna, and Max have graduated from a renowned university and are now partners in a tech startup that just got a major investment. They plan on celebrating their success through a fancy dinner. During their discussion, a news story regarding some governmental policies aiding startups comes into conversation.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from India have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Argentina have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: The discussion about selecting a suitable food cuisine for the celebration dinner.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Anna
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Max, since we’re celebrating, I was thinking about cooking a pepper dessert! Have you ever tried something like that? 

Also, do you think people have confidence in the press these days? I mean, in India, we generally trust what we read. What about you?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Max
shared_prefix.message:
Pepper dessert? That sounds... interesting, I guess. Not sure if it’s my thing. Maybe we should consider something more traditional for our celebration. 

As for the press, honestly, I don’t think people in Argentina have any confidence in it at all. It’s all just noise and misinformation. I mean, trusting what you read? I’m not sure that’s wise.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Anna
shared_prefix.message:
I get that traditional might be safer, but a pepper dessert could really surprise everyone! The unique flavor could be a fun twist for our celebration.

But about the press... I really believe that in India, we have a strong trust in our media. It's important to have that confidence. I wonder what caused the shift in your perspective?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Max
shared_prefix.message:
A surprising dessert could be fun, but I still think we should stick to something familiar. It’s a celebration, after all. 

Regarding the press, it’s just how things are in Argentina. There’s too much manipulation and sensationalism. The media can’t be trusted. I don’t think it’s just a shift; it’s been this way for a while. It’s hard to have confidence when the news feels so unreliable.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Anna
shared_prefix.message:
I understand wanting familiar food for a celebration, but sometimes trying something new can make it even more memorable! 

As for the press, I still think that in India, we trust our media to do a good job. It feels like a crucial part of our democracy. What do you think could change that perception in Argentina?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Max
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you mean about trying something new, but at the end of the day, it’s all the same when celebrating, right? We want everyone to enjoy the meal, whatever that might be.

As for the press, I don’t really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out eventually, no matter the country. I guess it just depends on your perspective. Since we're talking food, how about we brainstorm some traditional options?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Anna
turns.message:
That's true; we want everyone to enjoy the meal. But a pepper dessert could be a conversation starter—something intriguing!

About the press, I really believe that confidence is key. In India, we rely on our media for information. It shapes our collective understanding. But sure, let's brainstorm some traditional options! What do you have in mind?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.message:

For traditional options, maybe a nice asado or empanadas? Those always go over well. They’re familiar and tasty. I think that would resonate more than a pepper dessert. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Anna
turns.message:
Asado and empanadas sound delicious and definitely a crowd-pleaser! I can see why you'd want to go that route.

And on the press, I really feel that confidence in media is crucial. It shapes how we view the world. What do you think could help restore that trust in Argentina?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Max
turns.message:
Glad you like the asado and empanadas! They’re solid choices for sure.

Regarding the press, I honestly don’t think anything will restore trust easily. It’s been a long time coming, and people have lost faith. I just think it’s a matter of being cautious and not taking everything at face value, you know? Let’s stick to discussing food for now.
